description.narrative: The objective of the SME Competitiveness Project is to enhance the competitiveness and management capacity of targeted small and medium sized enterprises in Kazakhstan. There are four components to the project, the first component being SME capacity building program. The aim of this component is to introduce a coherent framework of SME capacity building programs to support competitiveness of all Kazakhstani firms regardless of size or sector. The second component is the SME linkages in competitive sectors. The objective of this component is to introduce a coherent framework to promote linkages and integration of SMEs in existing and emerging competitive sectors. The third component is the impact evaluation and monitoring of SME Programs. The aim of this component is to create a sustainable M&E structure that will shape SME policies and programs, helping to establish informed priorities and introduce midcourse corrections as required; as well as strengthening a sustainable Third-Party Monitoring System (TMS) that increases transparency and participation of the private sector and citizen engagement in SME policy design. Finally, the fourth component is the project management.
The project development objective is to enhance the competitiveness and capacity of targeted small and medium sized enterprises in Kazakhstan.

title.narrative: Value of increased sales of SMEs facilitated through participation in the project

comment.narrative:
<p>Achieved.</p>

<table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width:806px">
 <tbody>
  <tr>
   <td> Achievement of this target was supported by the SDP. Despite considerable success of the program, most participants were reluctant to disclose data on actual impact of their completed accreditations on their sales, revenues, and other business indicators. (And they were not under obligation to make such a disclosure.) At the end, only 15 participating SMEs (out of 53) reported back to the PIU on their incremental sales to large companies that were associated with their participation in the SDP. By all accounts, this is partial information that significantly underestimates the overall impact of the program on growth in SMEs sales. Moreover, it is worth mentioning that the full Impact of SDP-type program on sales is not immediate and is expected to materialize fully in the medium term.</td>
  </tr>
 </tbody>
</table>

title.narrative: Percentage of participating SMEs reporting improved management and business practices

comment.narrative:
<table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width:806px">
 <tbody>
  <tr>
   <td>Exceeded. This indicator was set for SMEs participating in both Component 1 and Subcomponent 2.1.  The assessment of actual progress was undertaken through three rounds of the survey of participating SMEs conducted through 2020. About 200 SMEs participated in each round.</td>
  </tr>
 </tbody>
</table>

title.narrative: Percent of training participants who found the training offered as effective and useful to them

comment.narrative:
<table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width:806px">
 <tbody>
  <tr>
   <td>Exceeded. Over the course of 2016-2021, about 289 participants of various training programs held under different project components (from both private sector and government agencies) found their training sessions to be effective and useful. This constitutes about 90.3% of of training participants that filled the questionnaire. The training modules were conducted on cluster development, supplier development, and M&E of SME support programs.</td>
  </tr>
 </tbody>
</table>

title.narrative: Beneficiaries who reported that the approaches discussed in the framework of the discussions held during the Project reflect their opinion

comment.narrative:
<table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width:806px">
 <tbody>
  <tr>
   <td>Achieved. This indicator tracked the share of project beneficiaries involved in project-sponsored events such as training seminars and policy roundtables, who agreed that the approaches, policy proposals and draft policy decisions discussed at these events reflected their views. The main emphasis in actual monitoring of the indicator was on the participants of private sector discussions over an appropriate for KZ model of the factoring platform. During 2019, the project sponsored a number of seminars and roundtables to discuss the options for factoring development with more than 600 (cumulatative number) SME representatives attending. On average for these events, 90,6% of the participants, who took part in the exit polls, agreed that the approaches discussed during the seminars reflected their views.</td>
  </tr>
 </tbody>
</table>

title.narrative: Strategic assessment for supply chain financing program has been completed, including recommendations on design, partners, structure, location, and regulatory requirements.

baseline.value: Activity is new and no prior experience is available in the country

target.value: Strategic assessment completed with clear and actionable recommendations on next steps for development of supply chain financing inthe country and factoring program installed.

comment.narrative:
<table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width:806px">
 <tbody>
  <tr>
   <td>Partially achieved. The feasibility study for the recommended factoring model was completed. The technical specifications for factoring platform’s software were prepared. However, the NBK did not assign the Central Securities Depository as the platform’s host, citing the need for further strengthening of the legal framework. Thus, procurement for the platform’s software was not launched. Nevertheless, the ToR and other supporting documentation for the platform development are available for the GoK to use once the enhanced legal framework is in place.</td>
  </tr>
 </tbody>
</table>

actual.value: Assessment with recommendations on all aspects of the terms of refence completed
